subject: Request: temporary rate ceiling uplift for Q3 pilot - Hartwell Medical
messages:
From: Alex Chan <alex.chan@hartwellmed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput spike next quarter — rate ceiling relief?

Hi Kimberly / Priyom,

Quick note from the Hartwell integrations team — we’re running a Q3 pilot that will route live clinical triage requests through Redwood’s hosted API. Forecast attached (Hartwell_traffic_forecast_Q3.xlsx). The pilot ramps in stages starting July 5 and we expect sustained 2.5x throughput vs our current baseline for an initial 30-day window, with short spikes up to ~6x for 10–14 minute intervals during morning triage.

Our current plan runs up against the hosted API rate ceiling and we’re concerned about automated throttling / fairness cuts during those short spikes. Can Redwood provide a temporary uplift to the rate ceiling or a shortburst policy for the pilot window so we avoid dropped requests? We need a solution that: 
- Guarantees no hard throttling during agreed windows, or a clear fallback model
- Has transparent logs for any fallback events
- Limits the uplift to a named window (we can provide exact dates) and a max QPS/cost cap

Contract/PO: HW-2027-PROD (procurement@hartwellmed.com is cc’d). Ideally we’d confirm by next week to lock our rollout timeline.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Chan
Director, Integrations — Hartwell Medical
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chan <alex.chan@hartwellmed.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput spike next quarter — rate ceiling relief?

Thanks Alex — this is helpful and the forecast attached gives us the shape we need. Short answers up front: we can do a time-bound uplift, with monitoring and agreed fallbacks. A few asks so we can scope the change cleanly: 

1) Exact pilot window (start/end) and any blackout dates.
2) Peak QPS target and 95th/99th percentile latency SLO you need preserved.
3) Whether you require guaranteed throughput (no throttling) or an increased fairness allocation (less aggressive tiebreak).

Immediate mitigations while we scope:
- Prefix caching on repeated prompts can cut token cost for many of your common flows.
- If you need strict guarantees, we can propose a short Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for the pilot — that’s heavier lift but removes hosted fairness constraints.

Priyom — can you draft an uplift proposal (72h/1-week/30-day options) with monitoring hooks and an escalation path? Alex — can Hartwell confirm exact dates so we can align capacity and billing guardrails?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Alex Chan <alex.chan@hartwellmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput spike next quarter — rate ceiling relief?

Alex / team — attaching a short proposal (rate-ceiling-proposal-2027-04-21.pdf) with three options: 

Option A — 72-hour targeted uplift window: +3x hosted rate ceiling for a named 72-hour window, automatic revert after window, cost cap enforced. Monitoring: token/req logs + alerting to Hartwell SRE and Redwood Ops.

Option B — 30-day guarded uplift: +2x sustained uplift, with automated fairness attenuation above a negotiated emergency threshold; weekly quality check-ins.

Option C — Short Dedicated pool trial: reserved GPU capacity for the pilot (preferred for zero-hosted throttling risk).

Operational notes: 
- We’ll create an RW ops ticket for realtime monitoring (RW-15432).
- Fallback behavior will be explicit in the runbook: if uplift exceeds the cost cap we auto-scale back to Option B parameters and send a 30-minute notice.
- For auditability, we emit a per-request header and store redacted traces for 90 days.

Marissa — can Sales Ops expedite a temporary uplift for the 72-hour model if Hartwell confirms dates? We’ll need Finance sign-off for the cost cap and Legal for a short amendment to the SLA.

Attachments: rate-ceiling-proposal-2027-04-21.pdf

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Chan <alex.chan@hartwellmed.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@hartwellmed.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput spike next quarter — rate ceiling relief?

Thanks Priyom — Option A (72-hour targeted uplift) looks like the best fit for our initial ramp. Confirming we’d like the uplift window: 2027-07-05 08:00 UTC through 2027-07-08 08:00 UTC. Peak target for the window: 3.5x baseline sustained with short spikes to 6x.

Two clarifications before we sign: 
- Please confirm that during the uplift window we will not be subject to fairness-driven decomms except in a declared emergency.
- What will the automatic revert notice look like (format and lead time)? We want a 30-minute warning and a post-window summary of any throttles/attenuations.

Procurement: PO is already in flight (HW-2027-PROD). If you need a billing contact I can loop in Sarah (procurement@hartwellmed.com).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — if you can send a DocuSign amendment with the selected Option A parameters we can get legal to review.

Best,
Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput spike next quarter — rate ceiling relief?

Looping in from Sales Ops: approved for a 72-hour uplift as described, pending a signed amendment. I’ve opened RW-15432 for ops monitoring and set a temporary cost cap of $12k for the window; Billing will not charge over the cap without explicit exec sign-off.

Action items: 
- Priyom: prepare runbook for the uplift window (alerts, who to page, toggle for auto-revert).
- Kimberly: send DocuSign link to Alex and CC legal.
- Alex / Hartwell: confirm PO and sign amendment by EOD Friday to meet provisioning lead time.

Quick note on revert behavior: we’ll emit a 30-minute pre-revert webhook and send a consolidated post-window report with per-minute throttling incidents (if any).

Marissa Cole
Sales Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
